title: GCS, AVPU, APGAR & PAT
body:
## Glasgow Coma Scale

Score each arm on its own, always report the three parts (`E3 V4 M5 = GCS 12`), and use the *best* response seen.

| Pts | Eye opening (adult) | Eye opening (peds under 2) |
|---|---|---|
| `4` | Spontaneous | Spontaneous |
| `3` | To voice | To voice / sound |
| `2` | To pain | To pain |
| `1` | None | None |

| Pts | Verbal (adult) | Verbal (peds under 2) |
|---|---|---|
| `5` | Oriented | Coos, babbles, smiles |
| `4` | Confused | Irritable cry, consolable |
| `3` | Inappropriate words | Cries to pain |
| `2` | Incomprehensible sounds | Moans to pain |
| `1` | None | None |

| Pts | Motor (adult) | Motor (peds under 2) |
|---|---|---|
| `6` | Obeys commands | Normal spontaneous movement |
| `5` | Localizes pain | Withdraws to touch |
| `4` | Withdraws from pain | Withdraws to pain |
| `3` | Flexion (decorticate) | Flexion (decorticate) |
| `2` | Extension (decerebrate) | Extension (decerebrate) |
| `1` | None | None |

Range `3–15`. Intubated patients score verbal as `1T`. Swollen-shut eyes score `1C`.

| Total | Severity |
|---|---|
| `13–15` | Mild |
| `9–12` | Moderate |
| `8 or less` | Severe — cannot protect the airway |

> **Key:** `GCS 8, intubate` is the classic line. Motor is the single most predictive arm.

## AVPU

| Letter | Means |
|---|---|
| `A` | Alert (add orientation: person, place, time, event = `A&O x4`) |
| `V` | Responds to verbal stimulus |
| `P` | Responds to painful stimulus only |
| `U` | Unresponsive |

Rough crosswalk: `A` about `15`, `V` about `12–13`, `P` about `8`, `U` about `3`.

## APGAR

Score the newborn at `1 minute` and `5 minutes`. If the 5-minute score is under `7`, repeat every `5 min` up to `20 min`. Never delay resuscitation to score.

| Sign | `0` | `1` | `2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A**ppearance (color) | Blue / pale all over | Body pink, limbs blue | Pink all over |
| **P**ulse | Absent | Under `100/min` | `100/min` or more |
| **G**rimace (reflex irritability) | No response | Grimace only | Cry, cough, sneeze, pulls away |
| **A**ctivity (tone) | Limp | Some flexion | Active motion |
| **R**espiration | Absent | Slow, weak, irregular cry | Strong cry |

| Total | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| `7–10` | Normal, routine care |
| `4–6` | Moderately depressed — stimulate, ventilate, reassess |
| `0–3` | Severely depressed — full resuscitation |

> **Trap:** APGAR does not decide whether to resuscitate. The three birth questions do: term? tone? breathing or crying?

## Pediatric Assessment Triangle

A doorway, hands-off, `15-second` impression. Abnormal on any arm means sick.

| Arm | Look for | Abnormal findings |
|---|---|---|
| **Appearance** (TICLS: Tone, Interactiveness, Consolability, Look/gaze, Speech/cry) | Brain perfusion | Limp, won't track, inconsolable, weak or absent cry |
| **Work of breathing** | Oxygenation / ventilation | Nasal flaring, retractions, head bobbing, grunting, tripod, abnormal sounds |
| **Circulation to skin** | Perfusion | Pallor, mottling, cyanosis |

| Pattern | Suggests |
|---|---|
| Appearance only | Primary brain / metabolic problem |
| Appearance + breathing | Respiratory failure |
| Appearance + circulation | Shock |
| All three | Cardiopulmonary failure — act now |
